target.name: RW Aurigae
target.summary_plain: A young star system, a few million years old, still wrapped in the disk of gas and dust it formed from. Clumps in that disk sometimes pass in front of the star, so its brightness changes without warning.

render.note: One asinh stretch per detector (0.5-99.7 percentiles of all its epochs), shared by every epoch, so brightness changes between frames are real. Co-adds: IMAGE minus ZODI, official photometry mask 0x3C028E44 rejected, OVERFLOW kept and flagged, then an inverse-variance mean after 3-sigma clipping (drops single-exposure streaks). Then vs Now: each image stretched by its own 0.5-99.7 percentiles. Differences: S/N, linear between the limits.

motion.method: Per-exposure ePSF position fits (D1-D6, S/N >= 10, 100 mas floor); sigma-clipped linear fit with parallax removed
motion.verdict_text: The fit gives 0.52 ± 0.07″ per year toward PA 78°, but Gaia DR3 says RW Aur A moves only 0.028″ per year. This is not real motion: RW Aur B, 1.5″ away at PA 74°, is unresolved by SPHEREx, and as A faded (by 0.86 mag at 3.8–4.4 µm) the combined light centre slid toward B. Astronomers call this variability-induced motion.

notes: Each point is one exposure: forced photometry at the catalogue position (ePSF fit, or a fit to the PSF wings when the core is saturated).
Saturated points are shown hollow and excluded from fits.
306 of 335 points are saturated (OVERFLOW in the core).
The quick-look curve is the Year-1 spectral cube at 12.9″ pixels: it blends close neighbours, and channels where the star saturates are left empty.

checks.name: proper-motion null test |mu| < 3 sigma
checks.value: 0.52 ± 0.07″/yr (7.9σ from zero) toward PA 78°: the unresolved companion lies at PA 74°, so this is a variability-induced photocentre shift, not motion

checks.name: brightness change > 0.2 mag at > 5 sigma at matched wavelengths (first vs last epoch)
checks.value: +0.86 ± 0.04 mag in D5 at 3.83–4.40 µm (23σ; positive = fading)

warnings: Saturated (OVERFLOW) in 306 of 335 exposures. Saturated pixels are kept in the images and outlined in the flags overlay; their brightness comes from fits to the PSF wings.
Variability-induced motion (VIM): RW Aur A and B (1.5″ apart) are unresolved, so the light centre moves toward B whenever A fades. The fitted proper motion is this shift, not motion of the star.
Blending: the A+B pair is measured as one source in every detector.
